title: VeriCoT: Neuro-symbolic Chain-of-Thought Validation via Logical Consistency Checks
claim: Each reasoning step is autoformalized into logic and checked against distilled, source-tagged premises, so flawed steps can be detected even when the answer is right.
layout: 3 colored panels, left-to-right; red arrows map steps to formulas, black arrows show implication
description: The figure shows a worked example of the verification procedure. At top left, a white box holds a source document and a question about whether Charlie qualifies for benefits. Below it, a red panel lists four input chain-of-thought steps C1–C4 in orange boxes. Red double arrows run from each step into a green panel containing first-order logic formulas F1–F4 in orange-outlined boxes. A blue panel at the top holds natural-language premises. Each premise has a purple tag (Commonsense, Context or Question) and links down to a matching blue-outlined logic premise P1–P3. Black arrows show logical implication from the premises and earlier formulas into each formula. A green check mark and the text 'VERIFIED' sit at the bottom. An 'Autoformalization' callout in red marks the translation step. Green 'Output' labels name the output regions.
caption: \method{} verification of a Chain-of-Thought for the SARA dataset [ref]. Even if the final answer is correct, a CoT that contains an invalid step hurts user trust and raises questions of LLM faithfulness. As shown in \S[ref], \method{} autoformalizes each step of the CoT into symbolic logic, producing a formula that ensures each one follows logically from a distilled list of NL premises, each of which it annotates with their source type (e.g. Commonsense or Context) If the CoT cannot be represented this way, it is unverifiable.
abstract: LLMs can perform multi-step reasoning through Chain-of-Thought (CoT), but they cannot reliably verify their own logic. Even when they reach correct answers, the underlying reasoning may be flawed, undermining trust in high-stakes scenarios. To mitigate this issue, we introduce VeriCoT, a neuro-symbolic method that extracts and verifies formal logical arguments from CoT reasoning. VeriCoT formalizes each CoT reasoning step into first-order logic and identifies premises that ground the argument in source context, commonsense knowledge, or prior reasoning steps. The symbolic representation enables automated solvers to verify logical validity while the NL premises allow humans and systems to identify ungrounded or fallacious reasoning steps. Experiments on the ProofWriter, LegalBench, and BioASQ datasets show VeriCoT effectively identifies flawed reasoning, and serves as a strong predictor of final answer correctness. We also leverage VeriCoT's verification signal for (1) inference-time self-reflection, (2) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on VeriCoT-distilled datasets and (3) preference fine-tuning (PFT) with direct preference optimization (DPO) using verification-based pairwise rewards, further improving reasoning validity and accuracy.
